set.body:
## Scope
Implement local activity models, schema migration, SQLite storage, event insertion, deduplication, and import checkpoints. Use standard-library SQLite WAL transactions and preserve the provenance contract from A0.

A local journal write failure may make presentation incomplete, but it must never recast an authoritative remote acceptance, scheduler observation, or validation receipt as a different outcome.

## Acceptance criteria
- Schema creation and forward migration are idempotent and preserve prior readable events.
- A transaction atomically records an event, its deduplication key, and the relevant import checkpoint; a crash leaves either all or none durable.
- Concurrent writers cannot create duplicate logical events or corrupt checkpoints.
- A repeated import is idempotent, retains original evidence provenance and timestamps, and makes its source/checkpoint inspectable.
- Retention and storage limits have a defined, testable policy, including observable `journal.degraded`/gap state rather than silent loss.
- Unit tests exercise transaction interruption, duplicate imports, concurrent writers, and storage-full or insert-failure behavior.
set.title: A1.1: implement a durable transactional SQLite activity journal
